full_article:
DHADING, Nepal (AP) — Workers shoveled thick mud from a flood-ravaged power station in central Nepal, trying to revive a key node that supplies electricity to more than 20,000 people. But as they cleared debris from equipment buried by last week’s catastrophic floods, there was hope the plant would not simply be rebuilt in the same place, beside the river that destroyed it.

In Nepal, up to 900 workers are unaccounted for from a dozen hydropower projects, according to the Independent Power Producers’ Association, Nepal, with hundreds believed trapped in tunnels. In Nepal and China combined, over 900 people have died and 4,700 are missing.

The loss of hydropower infrastructure is estimated to have taken 700 megawatts offline — about 10% of the country’s power capacity. Once the immediate aftermath of the disaster is dealt with, the question of how to restore power, roads, bridges, schools and health facilities quickly without rebuilding the same vulnerabilities should be on top of Nepalese authorities’ minds. disaster experts said.

They will also have to take a close look at other projects in Nepal that have not been built yet, whether they’ll be approved after this event,” said Jakob Steiner, a geoscientist at the University of Graz in Austria, who is currently based in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

Rebuilding for resilience, not just replacement

Hydropower projects that were operating or under construction were fully or partly destroyed across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading, among the worst-hit districts.

Many of the workers had taken shelter in the tunnels but are stuck, waiting to be rescued, according to officials.

“The tunnels are built to access hydropower infrastructure and to divert water,” Steiner said, describing the tunnels as big enough to drive trucks through.

Apart from the hydropower projects, tens of kilometers (miles) of roads, multiple bridges and essential buildings like schools and hospitals have been destroyed.

Ramraj Narasimhan, a senior director with the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure, said rebuilding should focus on continuity of services rather than trying to make every structure indestructible.

“If it gets damaged, let it get damaged, but can we build in redundancy in the system?” he said.

That can mean choosing a better location for construction, alternate routes, backup power, improved early warning and financial tools such as insurance to speed recovery, Narasimhan said. Risk assessments should examine where a river bends, where slopes are unstable and where a single failure could cut off several communities.

Narasimhan’s organization estimates that $124 billion worth of Nepal’s infrastructure is exposed to climate-driven disasters, creating the potential for hundreds of millions of dollars in losses each year. A report by the coalition earlier this year found that Nepal’s average annual losses are nearly $760 million from various disasters, while the country’s national disaster funds is only a fraction of this amount.

Climate risks grow for Himalayan hydropower

Climate scientists said the Himalayan region — which is warming faster than many other parts of the world — is particularly at risk from increasing global warming as a result of human-caused climate change.

Climate experts said the flooding adds to evidence that infrastructure planning in the Himalayas is being forced to account for disasters that are increasing as the climate warms. Glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya are losing ice at an accelerating rate, while permafrost degradation, unstable slopes, glacial lakes and increasingly erratic rainfall are raising the risks of floods, landslides and debris flows, according to reports by Kathmandu-based climate research group International Center for Integrated Mountain Development.

The stakes are particularly high for Nepal because hydropower is both a foundation of its electricity grid and an important source of economic growth and export revenue. Much of the country’s potential is run-of-river hydropower, Narasimhan said, meaning facilities are closely tied to steep river corridors where land is limited and hazards can cascade quickly.

Steiner said smaller floods can sometimes be managed with diversions that keep debris and high flows away from expensive infrastructure and tunnels. But for events as large as the latest flood, he said, physical defenses may be overwhelmed. In those cases, early warning becomes the critical protection for people.

He said the flood was detected at the China-Nepal border after moving rapidly from its source, leaving little warning time upstream. But there was still time as the flood traveled downstream toward hydropower sites, raising questions about whether warnings could have reached workers sooner.

The disaster is also likely to intensify scrutiny of where future projects are approved. Himanshu Thakkar, coordinator of the South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People, said environmental, social and disaster-risk assessments need to reflect the specific landscape and past hazards of each valley, backed by land-use rules and stronger accountability.

Hydropower projects can themselves become “force multipliers” when large structures, debris and altered river channels add to downstream damage, Thakkar said. He argued that Nepal should also consider more decentralized solar power as part of a broader energy mix.

title: Nepal floods expose risks to hydropower in a warming Himalayas - Bozeman Daily Chronicle
description: Nepal floods expose risks to hydropower in a warming Himalayas  Bozeman Daily Chronicle
publisher.title: Bozeman Daily Chronicle
full_article:
DHADING, Nepal (AP) — Workers shoveled thick mud from a flood-ravaged power station in central Nepal, trying to revive a key node that supplies electricity to more than 20,000 people. But as they cleared debris from equipment buried by last week's catastrophic floods, there was hope the plant would not simply be rebuilt in the same place, beside the river that destroyed it.

In Nepal, up to 900 workers are unaccounted for from a dozen hydropower projects, according to the Independent Power Producers’ Association, Nepal, with hundreds believed trapped in tunnels. In Nepal and China combined, over 900 people have died and 4,700 are missing.

The loss of hydropower infrastructure is estimated to have taken 700 megawatts offline — about 10% of the country’s power capacity. Once the immediate aftermath of the disaster is dealt with, the question of how to restore power, roads, bridges, schools and health facilities quickly without rebuilding the same vulnerabilities should be on top of Nepalese authorities' minds. disaster experts said.





“Authorities have to take a hard look in the mirror now and ask how they will be rebuilding in these places. They will also have to take a close look at other projects in Nepal that have not been built yet, whether they’ll be approved after this event,” said Jakob Steiner, a geoscientist at the University of Graz in Austria, who is currently based in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

Rebuilding for resilience, not just replacement

Hydropower projects that were operating or under construction were fully or partly destroyed across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading, among the worst-hit districts.

Many of the workers had taken shelter in the tunnels but are stuck, waiting to be rescued, according to officials.

“The tunnels are built to access hydropower infrastructure and to divert water,” Steiner said, describing the tunnels as big enough to drive trucks through.

Apart from the hydropower projects, tens of kilometers (miles) of roads, multiple bridges and essential buildings like schools and hospitals have been destroyed.

Ramraj Narasimhan, a senior director with the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure, said rebuilding should focus on continuity of services rather than trying to make every structure indestructible.

“If it gets damaged, let it get damaged, but can we build in redundancy in the system?” he said.

That can mean choosing a better location for construction, alternate routes, backup power, improved early warning and financial tools such as insurance to speed recovery, Narasimhan said. Risk assessments should examine where a river bends, where slopes are unstable and where a single failure could cut off several communities.

Narasimhan’s organization estimates that $124 billion worth of Nepal’s infrastructure is exposed to climate-driven disasters, creating the potential for hundreds of millions of dollars in losses each year. A report by the coalition earlier this year found that Nepal’s average annual losses are nearly $760 million from various disasters, while the country’s national disaster funds is only a fraction of this amount.

Climate risks grow for Himalayan hydropower

Climate scientists said the Himalayan region — which is warming faster than many other parts of the world — is particularly at risk from increasing global warming as a result of human-caused climate change.

Climate experts said the flooding adds to evidence that infrastructure planning in the Himalayas is being forced to account for disasters that are increasing as the climate warms. Glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya are losing ice at an accelerating rate, while permafrost degradation, unstable slopes, glacial lakes and increasingly erratic rainfall are raising the risks of floods, landslides and debris flows, according to reports by Kathmandu-based climate research group International Center for Integrated Mountain Development.

The stakes are particularly high for Nepal because hydropower is both a foundation of its electricity grid and an important source of economic growth and export revenue. Much of the country’s potential is run-of-river hydropower, Narasimhan said, meaning facilities are closely tied to steep river corridors where land is limited and hazards can cascade quickly.

Steiner said smaller floods can sometimes be managed with diversions that keep debris and high flows away from expensive infrastructure and tunnels. But for events as large as the latest flood, he said, physical defenses may be overwhelmed. In those cases, early warning becomes the critical protection for people.

He said the flood was detected at the China-Nepal border after moving rapidly from its source, leaving little warning time upstream. But there was still time as the flood traveled downstream toward hydropower sites, raising questions about whether warnings could have reached workers sooner.

The disaster is also likely to intensify scrutiny of where future projects are approved. Himanshu Thakkar, coordinator of the South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People, said environmental, social and disaster-risk assessments need to reflect the specific landscape and past hazards of each valley, backed by land-use rules and stronger accountability.

Hydropower projects can themselves become “force multipliers” when large structures, debris and altered river channels add to downstream damage, Thakkar said. He argued that Nepal should also consider more decentralized solar power as part of a broader energy mix.

Thakkar said the question now is not only how fast Nepal can rebuild, but what it chooses to put back in the path of the next flood.

नेपाल मे दर्जन भरि जलविद्युत परियोजना स 900 तक मजदूर क हिसाब नहि अछि, स्वतंत्र बिजली उत्पादक संघ, नेपाल क अनुसार सैकड़ों मजदूर सुरंग मे फंसल मानल जाइत अछि। नेपाल आ चीनमे मिला कए ९००सँ बेसी लोकक मृत्यु भेल अछि आ ४७०० गोटे लापता अछि ।

जलविद्युत बुनियादी ढाँचा केरऽ नुकसान के कारण ७०० मेगावाट ऑफलाइन होय ​​गेलऽ छै — देश केरऽ बिजली क्षमता केरऽ लगभग १०% । आपदा के तत्काल बाद के घटना स॑ निपटै के बाद वू ही कमजोरी के पुनर्निर्माण के बिना बिजली, सड़क, पुल, स्कूल आरू स्वास्थ्य सुविधा के जल्दी स॑ कोना बहाल करलऽ जाय, ई सवाल नेपाली अधिकारियऽ के दिमाग के ऊपर होना चाहियऽ । आपदा विशेषज्ञ कहलनि।





ऑस्ट्रिया केरऽ ग्राज विश्वविद्यालय केरऽ भूवैज्ञानिक जैकब स्टाइनर न॑ कहलकै कि अब॑ बांग्लादेश केरऽ ढाका म॑ स्थित आस्ट्रिया केरऽ ग्राज विश्वविद्यालय केरऽ भूवैज्ञानिक जैकब स्टाइनर न॑ कहलकै कि अधिकारियऽ क॑ अब॑ ऐना म॑ कड़ा नजर डालना छै आरू ई पूछना छै कि ई जगहऽ प॑ कोना पुनर्निर्माण करलऽ जैतै ।

लचीलापन के लेल पुनर्निर्माण, सिर्फ प्रतिस्थापन नहि

जलविद्युत परियोजना जे संचालित या निर्माणाधीन छल, पूरा या आंशिक रूप स नष्ट भ गेल छल, जे सबस बेसी प्रभावित जिला मे शामिल रसुवा, नुवाकोट आ धडिंग मे शामिल अछि।

अधिकारी सब के अनुसार बहुतो मजदूर सुरंग में शरण लेने छल मुदा फंसल अछि, बचाव के इंतजार में अछि।

स्टाइनर नँ कहलकै, “सुरंग जलविद्युत बुनियादी ढाँचा तक पहुँचै लेली आरू पानी क डायवर्ट करै लेली बनालौ गेलौ छै ।

जलविद्युत परियोजना क अलावा दसों किलोमीटर (मील) क सड़क, कईटा पुल आ स्कूल आ अस्पताल जेहन आवश्यक भवन नष्ट भ गेल अछि।

कोलिशन फॉर डिजास्टर रेजिलिएंट इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर केरऽ वरिष्ठ निदेशक रामराज नरसिंहन न॑ कहलकै कि पुनर्निर्माण म॑ हर संरचना क॑ अविनाशी बनाबै के कोशिश नै करी क॑ सेवा के निरंतरता प॑ ध्यान देना चाहियऽ ।

“जँ क्षतिग्रस्त भ’ गेल त’ क्षतिग्रस्त होब’ दियौक, मुदा की हम सभ सिस्टम मे रिडंडेंसी मे निर्माण क’ सकैत छी?” ओ कहलनि।

नरसिंहन नँ कहलकै कि एकरौ मतलब निर्माण लेली बेहतर स्थान, वैकल्पिक मार्ग, बैकअप पावर, बेहतर पूर्व चेतावनी आरू बीमा जैसनौ वित्तीय उपकरण चुनना हो सकै छै ताकि वसूली मँ तेजी आबी सकै । जोखिम आकलन मे इ जांच कैल जेबाक चाही की कोनों नदी कतय झुकएयत छै, कतय ढलान अस्थिर छै आ कतय एकटा विफलता कईटा समुदायक कें काटि सकय छै.

नरसिंहन केरऽ संगठन केरऽ अनुमान छै कि नेपाल केरऽ १२४ अरब डॉलर के बुनियादी ढाँचा जलवायु संचालित आपदा के सामना करै छै, जेकरा स॑ हर साल करोड़ों डॉलर के नुकसान के संभावना पैदा होय छै । गठबंधन केरऽ ई साल केरऽ शुरू म॑ जारी एगो रिपोर्ट म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि नेपाल केरऽ औसत वार्षिक नुकसान विभिन्न आपदा स॑ लगभग ७६ करोड़ डॉलर होय छै, जबकि देश केरऽ राष्ट्रीय आपदा निधि ई राशि केरऽ कुछ हिस्सा ही छै ।

हिमालयी जलविद्युत के लेल जलवायु के जोखिम बढ़ैत अछि

जलवायु वैज्ञानिकऽ न॑ कहलकै कि हिमालयी क्षेत्र – जे दुनिया केरऽ बहुत सारा अन्य भागऽ के तुलना म॑ तेजी स॑ गरम होय रहलऽ छै – मानव के कारण जलवायु परिवर्तन के परिणामस्वरूप बढ़तऽ ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के खास तौर प॑ खतरा म॑ छै ।

जलवायु विशेषज्ञऽ न॑ कहलकै कि बाढ़ स॑ ई बात के सबूत आरू बढ़ी जाय छै कि हिमालय म॑ बुनियादी ढाँचा के योजना क॑ जलवायु गरम होय के साथ बढ़त॑ जाय रहलऽ आपदा के हिसाब दै लेली मजबूर करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै । काठमांडू स्थित जलवायु अनुसंधान समूह इंटरनेशनल सेंटर फॉर इंटीग्रेटेड माउंटेन डेवलपमेंट केरऽ रिपोर्ट के अनुसार हिन्दू कुश हिमालय केरऽ पूरा ग्लेशियरऽ म॑ तेजी स॑ बर्फ के नुकसान होय ​​रहलऽ छै, जबकि पर्माफ्रॉस्ट केरऽ क्षरण, अस्थिर ढलान, ग्लेशियल झील आरू बढ़त॑-बढ़त॑ अव्यवस्थित वर्षा के कारण बाढ़, भूस्खलन आरू मलबा के बहाव के खतरा बढ़ी रहलऽ छै ।

नेपाल के लेल विशेष रूप स दांव बेसी अछि किया कि जलविद्युत ओकर बिजली ग्रिड के आधार आ आर्थिक विकास आ निर्यात राजस्व के महत्वपूर्ण स्रोत दुनु अछि। नरसिंहन न॑ कहलकै कि देश केरऽ बहुत संभावना रन-ऑफ-रिवर जलविद्युत छै, मतलब सुविधा खड़ी नदी गलियारा स॑ गहराई स॑ जुड़लऽ छै, जहां जमीन सीमित छै आरू खतरा जल्दी स॑ झरना बनी सकै छै ।

स्टाइनर न॑ कहलकै कि छोटऽ बाढ़ क॑ कखनी-कखनी डायवर्सन स॑ प्रबंधित करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै जेकरा स॑ मलबा आरू उच्च प्रवाह क॑ महंगा बुनियादी ढाँचा आरू सुरंग स॑ दूर रखलऽ जाय सकै छै । मुदा ताजा बाढ़ि जेहन पैघ आयोजन लेल ओ कहला जे शारीरिक रक्षा पर भारी पड़ि सकैत अछि। ओहि मामला मे जल्दी चेतावनी लोकक लेल महत्वपूर्ण सुरक्षा बनि जाइत अछि ।

ओ कहलनि जे, बाढ़िक स्रोत सं तेजी सं बढ़ला के बाद चीन-नेपाल सीमा पर पता चलल, जाहि सं अपस्ट्रीम मे चेतावनी देबय के समय कम रहि गेल अछि. लेकिन अभी भी समय छेलै, कैन्हेंकि बाढ़ नीचें जलविद्युत स्थल के तरफ जाय रहलऽ छेलै, जेकरा स॑ ई सवाल उठी रहलऽ छेलै कि की चेतावनी मजदूरऽ तलक जल्दी पहुँची सकै छेलै ।

संभावना अछि जे एहि आपदा स इ जांच सेहो तेज भ जाएत जे भविष्य मे परियोजना कए कतए मंजूरी देल जाएत। दक्षिण एशिया नेटवर्क ऑन डैम्स, रिवर्स एंड पीपुल के समन्वयक हिमांशु ठक्कर नँ कहलकै कि पर्यावरण, सामाजिक आरू आपदा-जोखिम के आकलन मँ हर घाटी के विशिष्ट परिदृश्य आरू पिछला खतरा क प्रतिबिंबित करै के जरूरत छै, जेकरा मँ भूमि उपयोग के नियम आरू मजबूत जवाबदेही के समर्थन मिलै छै ।

ठक्कर न॑ कहलकै कि जलविद्युत परियोजना खुद “फोर्स मल्टीप्लायर” बनी सकै छै जब॑ बड़ऽ संरचना, मलबा आरू बदललऽ नदी चैनल नीचें के नुकसान म॑ वृद्धि करै छै । हुनकऽ तर्क छेलै कि नेपाल क॑ भी व्यापक ऊर्जा मिश्रण के हिस्सा के रूप म॑ अधिक विकेंद्रीकृत सौर ऊर्जा प॑ विचार करना चाहियऽ ।

ठक्कर कहलनि जे, आब सवाल इ नहि अछि जे नेपाल कतेक तेजी सं पुनर्निर्माण क सकैत अछि, बल्कि अगिला बाढ़िक बाट मे फेर सं की राखय लेल की चुनैत अछि।

title: Nepal floods expose risks to hydropower in a warming Himalayas | National News | 2news.com - KTVN
description: Nepal floods expose risks to hydropower in a warming Himalayas | National News | 2news.com  KTVN
publisher.title: KTVN
full_article:
DHADING, Nepal (AP) — Workers shoveled thick mud from a flood-ravaged power station in central Nepal, trying to revive a key node that supplies electricity to more than 20,000 people. But as they cleared debris from equipment buried by last week's catastrophic floods, there was hope the plant would not simply be rebuilt in the same place, beside the river that destroyed it.

In Nepal, up to 900 workers are unaccounted for from a dozen hydropower projects, according to the Independent Power Producers’ Association, Nepal, with hundreds believed trapped in tunnels. In Nepal and China combined, over 900 people have died and 4,700 are missing.

The loss of hydropower infrastructure is estimated to have taken 700 megawatts offline — about 10% of the country’s power capacity. Once the immediate aftermath of the disaster is dealt with, the question of how to restore power, roads, bridges, schools and health facilities quickly without rebuilding the same vulnerabilities should be on top of Nepalese authorities' minds. disaster experts said.

“Authorities have to take a hard look in the mirror now and ask how they will be rebuilding in these places. They will also have to take a close look at other projects in Nepal that have not been built yet, whether they’ll be approved after this event,” said Jakob Steiner, a geoscientist at the University of Graz in Austria, who is currently based in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

Rebuilding for resilience, not just replacement

Hydropower projects that were operating or under construction were fully or partly destroyed across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading, among the worst-hit districts.

Many of the workers had taken shelter in the tunnels but are stuck, waiting to be rescued, according to officials.

“The tunnels are built to access hydropower infrastructure and to divert water,” Steiner said, describing the tunnels as big enough to drive trucks through.

Apart from the hydropower projects, tens of kilometers (miles) of roads, multiple bridges and essential buildings like schools and hospitals have been destroyed.

Ramraj Narasimhan, a senior director with the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure, said rebuilding should focus on continuity of services rather than trying to make every structure indestructible.

“If it gets damaged, let it get damaged, but can we build in redundancy in the system?” he said.

That can mean choosing a better location for construction, alternate routes, backup power, improved early warning and financial tools such as insurance to speed recovery, Narasimhan said. Risk assessments should examine where a river bends, where slopes are unstable and where a single failure could cut off several communities.

Narasimhan’s organization estimates that $124 billion worth of Nepal’s infrastructure is exposed to climate-driven disasters, creating the potential for hundreds of millions of dollars in losses each year. A report by the coalition earlier this year found that Nepal’s average annual losses are nearly $760 million from various disasters, while the country’s national disaster funds is only a fraction of this amount.

Climate risks grow for Himalayan hydropower

Climate scientists said the Himalayan region — which is warming faster than many other parts of the world — is particularly at risk from increasing global warming as a result of human-caused climate change.

Climate experts said the flooding adds to evidence that infrastructure planning in the Himalayas is being forced to account for disasters that are increasing as the climate warms. Glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya are losing ice at an accelerating rate, while permafrost degradation, unstable slopes, glacial lakes and increasingly erratic rainfall are raising the risks of floods, landslides and debris flows, according to reports by Kathmandu-based climate research group International Center for Integrated Mountain Development.

The stakes are particularly high for Nepal because hydropower is both a foundation of its electricity grid and an important source of economic growth and export revenue. Much of the country’s potential is run-of-river hydropower, Narasimhan said, meaning facilities are closely tied to steep river corridors where land is limited and hazards can cascade quickly.

Steiner said smaller floods can sometimes be managed with diversions that keep debris and high flows away from expensive infrastructure and tunnels. But for events as large as the latest flood, he said, physical defenses may be overwhelmed. In those cases, early warning becomes the critical protection for people.

He said the flood was detected at the China-Nepal border after moving rapidly from its source, leaving little warning time upstream. But there was still time as the flood traveled downstream toward hydropower sites, raising questions about whether warnings could have reached workers sooner.

The disaster is also likely to intensify scrutiny of where future projects are approved. Himanshu Thakkar, coordinator of the South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People, said environmental, social and disaster-risk assessments need to reflect the specific landscape and past hazards of each valley, backed by land-use rules and stronger accountability.

Hydropower projects can themselves become “force multipliers” when large structures, debris and altered river channels add to downstream damage, Thakkar said. He argued that Nepal should also consider more decentralized solar power as part of a broader energy mix.

Thakkar said the question now is not only how fast Nepal can rebuild, but what it chooses to put back in the path of the next flood.

जलविद्युत बुनियादी ढाँचा केरऽ नुकसान के कारण ७०० मेगावाट ऑफलाइन होय ​​गेलऽ छै — देश केरऽ बिजली क्षमता केरऽ लगभग १०% । आपदा के तत्काल बाद के घटना स॑ निपटै के बाद वू ही कमजोरी के पुनर्निर्माण के बिना बिजली, सड़क, पुल, स्कूल आरू स्वास्थ्य सुविधा के जल्दी स॑ कोना बहाल करलऽ जाय, ई सवाल नेपाली अधिकारियऽ के दिमाग के ऊपर होना चाहियऽ । आपदा विशेषज्ञ कहलनि।

ऑस्ट्रिया केरऽ ग्राज विश्वविद्यालय केरऽ भूवैज्ञानिक जैकब स्टाइनर न॑ कहलकै कि अब॑ बांग्लादेश केरऽ ढाका म॑ स्थित आस्ट्रिया केरऽ ग्राज विश्वविद्यालय केरऽ भूवैज्ञानिक जैकब स्टाइनर न॑ कहलकै कि अधिकारियऽ क॑ अब॑ ऐना म॑ कड़ा नजर डालना छै आरू ई पूछना छै कि ई जगहऽ प॑ कोना पुनर्निर्माण करलऽ जैतै ।

लचीलापन के लेल पुनर्निर्माण, सिर्फ प्रतिस्थापन नहि

जलविद्युत परियोजना जे संचालित या निर्माणाधीन छल, पूरा या आंशिक रूप स नष्ट भ गेल छल, जे सबस बेसी प्रभावित जिला मे शामिल रसुवा, नुवाकोट आ धडिंग मे शामिल अछि।

अधिकारी सब के अनुसार बहुतो मजदूर सुरंग में शरण लेने छल मुदा फंसल अछि, बचाव के इंतजार में अछि।

स्टाइनर नँ कहलकै, “सुरंग जलविद्युत बुनियादी ढाँचा तक पहुँचै लेली आरू पानी क डायवर्ट करै लेली बनालौ गेलौ छै ।

जलविद्युत परियोजना क अलावा दसों किलोमीटर (मील) क सड़क, कईटा पुल आ स्कूल आ अस्पताल जेहन आवश्यक भवन नष्ट भ गेल अछि।

कोलिशन फॉर डिजास्टर रेजिलिएंट इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर केरऽ वरिष्ठ निदेशक रामराज नरसिंहन न॑ कहलकै कि पुनर्निर्माण म॑ हर संरचना क॑ अविनाशी बनाबै के कोशिश नै करी क॑ सेवा के निरंतरता प॑ ध्यान देना चाहियऽ ।

“जँ क्षतिग्रस्त भ’ गेल त’ क्षतिग्रस्त होब’ दियौक, मुदा की हम सभ सिस्टम मे रिडंडेंसी मे निर्माण क’ सकैत छी?” ओ कहलनि।

नरसिंहन नँ कहलकै कि एकरौ मतलब निर्माण लेली बेहतर स्थान, वैकल्पिक मार्ग, बैकअप पावर, बेहतर पूर्व चेतावनी आरू बीमा जैसनौ वित्तीय उपकरण चुनना हो सकै छै ताकि वसूली मँ तेजी आबी सकै । जोखिम आकलन मे इ जांच कैल जेबाक चाही की कोनों नदी कतय झुकएयत छै, कतय ढलान अस्थिर छै आ कतय एकटा विफलता कईटा समुदायक कें काटि सकय छै.

नरसिंहन केरऽ संगठन केरऽ अनुमान छै कि नेपाल केरऽ १२४ अरब डॉलर के बुनियादी ढाँचा जलवायु संचालित आपदा के सामना करै छै, जेकरा स॑ हर साल करोड़ों डॉलर के नुकसान के संभावना पैदा होय छै । गठबंधन केरऽ ई साल केरऽ शुरू म॑ जारी एगो रिपोर्ट म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि नेपाल केरऽ औसत वार्षिक नुकसान विभिन्न आपदा स॑ लगभग ७६ करोड़ डॉलर होय छै, जबकि देश केरऽ राष्ट्रीय आपदा निधि ई राशि केरऽ कुछ हिस्सा ही छै ।

हिमालयी जलविद्युत के लेल जलवायु के जोखिम बढ़ैत अछि

जलवायु वैज्ञानिकऽ न॑ कहलकै कि हिमालयी क्षेत्र – जे दुनिया केरऽ बहुत सारा अन्य भागऽ के तुलना म॑ तेजी स॑ गरम होय रहलऽ छै – मानव के कारण जलवायु परिवर्तन के परिणामस्वरूप बढ़तऽ ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के खास तौर प॑ खतरा म॑ छै ।

जलवायु विशेषज्ञऽ न॑ कहलकै कि बाढ़ स॑ ई बात के सबूत आरू बढ़ी जाय छै कि हिमालय म॑ बुनियादी ढाँचा के योजना क॑ जलवायु गरम होय के साथ बढ़त॑ जाय रहलऽ आपदा के हिसाब दै लेली मजबूर करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै । काठमांडू स्थित जलवायु अनुसंधान समूह इंटरनेशनल सेंटर फॉर इंटीग्रेटेड माउंटेन डेवलपमेंट केरऽ रिपोर्ट के अनुसार हिन्दू कुश हिमालय केरऽ पूरा ग्लेशियरऽ म॑ तेजी स॑ बर्फ के नुकसान होय ​​रहलऽ छै, जबकि पर्माफ्रॉस्ट केरऽ क्षरण, अस्थिर ढलान, ग्लेशियल झील आरू बढ़त॑-बढ़त॑ अव्यवस्थित वर्षा के कारण बाढ़, भूस्खलन आरू मलबा के बहाव के खतरा बढ़ी रहलऽ छै ।

नेपाल के लेल विशेष रूप स दांव बेसी अछि किया कि जलविद्युत ओकर बिजली ग्रिड के आधार आ आर्थिक विकास आ निर्यात राजस्व के महत्वपूर्ण स्रोत दुनु अछि। नरसिंहन न॑ कहलकै कि देश केरऽ बहुत संभावना रन-ऑफ-रिवर जलविद्युत छै, मतलब सुविधा खड़ी नदी गलियारा स॑ गहराई स॑ जुड़लऽ छै, जहां जमीन सीमित छै आरू खतरा जल्दी स॑ झरना बनी सकै छै ।

स्टाइनर न॑ कहलकै कि छोटऽ बाढ़ क॑ कखनी-कखनी डायवर्सन स॑ प्रबंधित करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै जेकरा स॑ मलबा आरू उच्च प्रवाह क॑ महंगा बुनियादी ढाँचा आरू सुरंग स॑ दूर रखलऽ जाय सकै छै । मुदा ताजा बाढ़ि जेहन पैघ आयोजन लेल ओ कहला जे शारीरिक रक्षा पर भारी पड़ि सकैत अछि। ओहि मामला मे जल्दी चेतावनी लोकक लेल महत्वपूर्ण सुरक्षा बनि जाइत अछि ।

ओ कहलनि जे, बाढ़िक स्रोत सं तेजी सं बढ़ला के बाद चीन-नेपाल सीमा पर पता चलल, जाहि सं अपस्ट्रीम मे चेतावनी देबय के समय कम रहि गेल अछि. लेकिन अभी भी समय छेलै, कैन्हेंकि बाढ़ नीचें जलविद्युत स्थल के तरफ जाय रहलऽ छेलै, जेकरा स॑ ई सवाल उठी रहलऽ छेलै कि की चेतावनी मजदूरऽ तलक जल्दी पहुँची सकै छेलै ।

संभावना अछि जे एहि आपदा स इ जांच सेहो तेज भ जाएत जे भविष्य मे परियोजना कए कतए मंजूरी देल जाएत। दक्षिण एशिया नेटवर्क ऑन डैम्स, रिवर्स एंड पीपुल के समन्वयक हिमांशु ठक्कर नँ कहलकै कि पर्यावरण, सामाजिक आरू आपदा-जोखिम के आकलन मँ हर घाटी के विशिष्ट परिदृश्य आरू पिछला खतरा क प्रतिबिंबित करै के जरूरत छै, जेकरा मँ भूमि उपयोग के नियम आरू मजबूत जवाबदेही के समर्थन मिलै छै ।

ठक्कर न॑ कहलकै कि जलविद्युत परियोजना खुद “फोर्स मल्टीप्लायर” बनी सकै छै जब॑ बड़ऽ संरचना, मलबा आरू बदललऽ नदी चैनल नीचें के नुकसान म॑ वृद्धि करै छै । हुनकऽ तर्क छेलै कि नेपाल क॑ भी व्यापक ऊर्जा मिश्रण के हिस्सा के रूप म॑ अधिक विकेंद्रीकृत सौर ऊर्जा प॑ विचार करना चाहियऽ ।

ठक्कर कहलनि जे, आब सवाल इ नहि अछि जे नेपाल कतेक तेजी सं पुनर्निर्माण क सकैत अछि, बल्कि अगिला बाढ़िक बाट मे फेर सं की राखय लेल की चुनैत अछि।

सिबी अरसु बेंगलुरु स रिपोर्ट केलनि आ एक्स पर @sibi123 पर फॉलो कएल जा सकैत अछि। हुनका स sarasu@ap.org पर संपर्क करू।

एसोसिएटेड प्रेस कें जलवायु आ पर्यावरण कवरेज कें कईटा निजी फाउंडेशनक सं आर्थिक सहायता भेटैत छै. सब सामग्री के लेल एपी के जिम्मेदारी मात्र अछि। परोपकार कें साथ काम करय कें लेल एपी कें मानक, समर्थक कें सूची आ वित्त पोषित कवरेज क्षेत्रक कें एपी.ओआरजी पर खोजूं.

description: Live updates: Sharp rise in number of people missing in Nepal as floods death toll exceeds 900  CNNNepal-Tibet flood death toll surpasses 900, officials say, more than 4,700 missing  ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and VideosHundreds of workers feared stuck in hydropower tunnels as Nepal flood deaths cross 900  AP News
publisher.title: CNN
full_article:
Video from the Nepali army released on Sunday shows rescue teams attempting to save workers trapped in Nuwakot's hydro power plant. Rescuers drilled at the tunnels to send trapped workers food and oxygen masks. Nepali Army

Rescue teams began rappelling into a tunnel at a hydropower plant in Nepal late Sunday, as part of an urgent mission to search for survivors who might be trapped inside several days after the devastating flash flood.

A roughly two-feet-wide hole has been drilled through the heavily fortified exterior of the tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-3A hydropower project, officials said, adding that rescue teams were hoping to get inside to identify where in the kilometers-long tunnel the workers might be.

They “descended through the opening using ropes and called out to those trapped inside, but received no response,” the prime minister’s office said on Sunday.

Video showed the workers rappelling downward into the dark cavern, wearing harnesses and helmets.

“Preparations have reached the final stage for sending rescue personnel into the tunnel equipped with oxygen, medical supplies, communication equipment, and cameras,” said the Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation in a news release on Sunday.

“The team is preparing to reach the suspected working space approximately 180 meters inside the tunnel from the portal, where it will assess the actual conditions, determine the possible location of the trapped individuals, and evaluate the safety situation as accurately as possible.”

Earlier, the team had also pumped air into the tunnel, and sent food inside.

A total of 90 personnel are on site, including from the Nepal Army, Nepal Police and the Armed Police Force, as well as sniffer dogs and search-and-rescue teams, officials said.

Foreign rescue teams are working to clear and search other hydropower projects, which are scattered along the Trishuli river winding through multiple districts. The Indian team, for instance, is monitoring the Chilime and Langtang areas by helicopter, while the Chinese team has already searched the tunnel of the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, said the ministry’s news release.

Authorities met with the families of missing workers on Sunday, and told them the government “is leaving no stone unturned to save the lives of its citizens,” the ministry added.
translated:
रविदिन जारी नेपाली सेनाके विडियोमे बचाव दल नुवाकोटके जल विद्युत संयंत्रमे फँसल मजदूरके बचेबाक प्रयासरत देखल जा रहल अछि । बचावकर्मी सुरंग पर ड्रिल कए फंसल मजदूर कए भोजन आ ऑक्सीजन मास्क पठेलक। नेपाली सेना

नेपाल केरऽ एगो जलविद्युत संयंत्र केरऽ सुरंग म॑ रविवार देर रात बचाव दल रेपलिंग शुरू करी देलकै, जे विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ के बाद कई दिन बाद भीतर फंसलऽ रह॑ सकै वाला बची गेलऽ लोगऽ के खोज करै के तत्काल मिशन के तहत छै ।

अधिकारी नँ कहलकै कि अपर त्रिशुली-3ए जलविद्युत परियोजना मँ सुरंग केरौ भारी किलाबंदी वाला बाहरी हिस्सा के माध्यम स॑ मोटा-मोटी दू फीट चौड़ा छेद ड्रिल करलऽ गेलऽ छै, आरू कहलकै कि बचाव टीम क॑ उम्मीद छै कि वू अंदर घुसी क॑ ई पहचान करी सकै छै कि किलोमीटर लंबा सुरंग म॑ मजदूर कहाँ होय सकै छै ।

प्रधानमंत्री कार्यालय न॑ रविवार क॑ कहलकै कि हुनी “रस्सी के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ खुललऽ जगह स॑ उतरी क॑ भीतर फंसलऽ लोगऽ क॑ आवाज देलकै, लेकिन ओकरा कोनो प्रतिक्रिया नै मिललै ।

वीडियो मे देखाओल गेल अछि जे मजदूर हार्नेस आ हेलमेट पहिरने अन्हार गुफा मे नीचा दिस रैपल करैत छल।

ऊर्जा, जल संसाधन आरू सिंचाई मंत्रालय नँ रविवार क जारी एगो समाचार विज्ञप्ति जारी करी क कहलकै कि ऑक्सीजन, चिकित्सा आपूर्ति, संचार उपकरण, आरू कैमरा स॑ लैस सुरंग म॑ बचाव कर्मी क॑ भेजै के तैयारी अंतिम चरण म॑ पहुँची गेलऽ छै ।

“टीम पोर्टल स॑ सुरंग के अंदर लगभग १८० मीटर दूर संदिग्ध काम के जगह प॑ पहुँचै के तैयारी करी रहलऽ छै, जहां वू वास्तविक स्थिति के आकलन करतै, फंसलऽ व्यक्तियऽ के संभावित स्थान के निर्धारण करतै, आरू सुरक्षा केरऽ स्थिति के यथासंभव सटीक मूल्यांकन करतै।”

एहि स पहिने टीम सुरंग मे हवा सेहो पंप कएने छल, आ भोजन कए अंदर पठा देने छल।

अधिकारी सब कहलनि जे, नेपाली सेना, नेपाल प्रहरी आ सशस्त्र प्रहरी बल सहित कुल ९० जवान स्थल पर अछि, संगहि सुंघनिहार कुकुर आ खोज-बचाव दल सेहो शामिल अछि।

विदेशी बचाव टीम अन्य जलविद्युत परियोजना क॑ खाली करै आरू खोज करै के काम करी रहलऽ छै, जे कई जिला स॑ घुमावदार त्रिशुली नदी के किनारे बिखरी गेलऽ छै । मंत्रालय केरऽ समाचार विज्ञप्ति म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि भारतीय टीम, उदाहरण लेली चिलीमे आरू लैंगटांग क्षेत्रऽ प॑ हेलीकॉप्टर स॑ नजर रखी रहलऽ छै, जबकि चीनी टीम न॑ अपर त्रिशुली-१ जलविद्युत परियोजना केरऽ सुरंग के तलाशी लेन॑ छै ।

मंत्रालय न॑ आरू कहलकै कि रविवार क॑ अधिकारियऽ न॑ लापता मजदूरऽ के परिवारऽ स॑ भेंट करलकै, आरू कहलकै कि सरकार “अपनऽ नागरिकऽ के जान बचाबै लेली कोय पत्थर नै छोड़ी रहलऽ छै ।

title: First Thing: Desperate rescue attempts continue in Nepal to reach hundreds thought to be trapped - The Guardian
description: First Thing: Desperate rescue attempts continue in Nepal to reach hundreds thought to be trapped  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
Good morning. Rescue teams are working to reach hundreds of people feared trapped in the tunnels and underground areas of half a dozen hydropower projects in Nepal as more than 900 workers were reported missing after the devastating flash floods.

The death toll from the ⁠unprecedented deluge of ice, rock, mud ​and debris that crashed through valleys of Nepal on Wednesday last week has risen to 903 people, with 16 reported dead on the Tibet side of the border. More than 4,000 are missing in Nepal, with another 500 in Tibet. Hundreds of bodies, many unidentified, have been buried in shallow graves.

How large is the rescue operation? Nepal’s prime minister, Balendra Shah, said almost 21,000 security personnel were involved in the rescue operations, besides civilian workers and volunteers. China’s state-run CCTV reported that Beijing had mobilised more than 2,100 rescue workers. The Red Cross has ‌estimated that more than 90,000 people are likely to have been affected by the disaster, which China and some experts linked to the effects of the climate crisis.

Why has the disaster sparked a racism row in Australia? A slew of racist social media comments have been made towards missing Australians. Most of them were on pilgrimages, including to Mount Kailash in Tibet. Mainstream media outlets including News Corp, Channel 7, Channel 10 and Nine have been hit with highly offensive and discriminatory comments on Facebook articles identifying the missing Australians.

US strikes Iranian launchers in strait of Hormuz, sparking reprisal attack on airbases in Jordan and UAE

View image in fullscreen A wide view of the northern part of the strait of Hormuz, showing the islands of Hormuz (R), Larak (C), and Qeshm (L). Photograph: Satellite image ©2020 Maxar Tech/AFP/Getty Images

Iran has launched retaliatory strikes on airbases in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates after the US attacked Iranian rocket launchers in the strait of Hormuz, the first such hostilities in a month. The last known ‌US strikes on Iran were in late July and the war has reached a stalemate in recent weeks.

The latest exchange of fire was sparked late on Sunday by a US attack on the island of Larak in the strait. Iran’s ⁠Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said the US attack killed and wounded several soldiers and citizens and ​would be met with “punishment” from ‌Tehran.

What has Donald Trump claimed US forces are doing? Hours after the attacks, the US president, Donald Trump, claimed in a social media post that Iran’s energy hub of Kharg Island was being “blown to smithereens” but gave no further details. The White House and ⁠the US defense department did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Attacking Kharg, which handled 90% of ⁠Iran’s oil exports before the war, would severely disrupt the Islamic republic’s energy trade and put huge pressure on its economy.

Canada erects giant ‘Lake Ontario’ sign as spat with Trump over name escalates

View image in fullscreen The Lake Ontario sign. Photograph: Carlos Osorio/Reuters

Donald Trump and Canada continued a verbal duel at the weekend over the US government’s administrative renaming of Lake Ontario, with the Ontario premier erecting a giant sign saying “Lake Ontario. Now and Always” – and the American president posting an AI video depicting him tearing down an avatar of that sign, erecting a replacement saying Lake America, and dancing to YMCA.

The Wendat Nation grand chief, Pierre Picard, called Trump’s move an attempt to erase Indigenous history. “I want to tell him that it is unacceptable for us, as a nation, to have a president who can eradicate our history, our culture and our identity,” Picard said.

Trump ‘border czar’ denies Milo Yiannopoulos was deported quickly to spare him from ICE detention

Milo Yiannopoulos after his arrest by federal immigration agents. Photograph: Department of Homeland Security/Reuters

The White House “border czar”, Tom Homan, denied on Sunday that deporting the British far-right commentator Milo Yiannopoulos just a day after being arrested by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) amounted to preferential treatment.

Homan said it was his understanding Yiannopoulos, 41, had overstayed what he believed to be a visitor visa, had not appeared at an immigration hearing and was issued a final order of removal on 22 July. He added: “He had his due process, ordered removed by a federal judge, and ICE removed him. It’s that simple.”

In other news …

View image in fullscreen NBC’s Kristen Welker. Photograph: Jim Bourg/Reuters

Donald Trump ⁠said NBC’s Kristen ‌Welker should face “rebuke or punishment” from the FCC after she described the success record of political candidates whom the president had endorsed as “mixed”.

Ghislaine Maxwell has virtually run out of legal routes to overturn her conviction for her involvement in Jeffrey Epstein’s abuse of girls and young women, experts say, bar a presidential pardon.

At least eight people have died off the coast of Turkish-occupied northern Cyprus after a ferry capsized . Nearly 20 people are still missing.

The Trump administration is shuttering ⁠two of the three US Department of Agriculture research projects studying cyclospora after the foodborne parasite has ⁠sickened tens of thousands of Americans during the summer.

Michigan’s Democratic US senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed apologized to the state’s Jewish Democratic Caucus for comments he made after an attack on a synagogue in March, which he tied to Israel’s actions in the Middle East.

Stat of the day: Discount gas stations praised by Trump sold $4m of stolen fuel, lawsuit claims

View image in fullscreen A flag flies at Freedom Fuel Network gas station. Photograph: Matt Rourke/AP

Mansfield Oil Company of Gainesville is suing KRSM and its president, Syed Kazmi, for allegedly picking up nearly $4m of fuel and not paying for it. KRSM sold some of the fuel to stations that are part of the Freedom Fuel Network, promoted by the Trump administration when drivers were facing higher oil prices amid the war with Iran.

Building Power: How two Indiana tribes drove out a mining company in one week

View image in fullscreen An oil pump jack. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images

At the sacred prairie of Pe’ Sla in South Dakota, Indigenous and environmental groups banded together to halt drilling. “We’re just not used to winning,” said Dr Valeriah Big Eagle, who directs the Black Hills work of NDN Collective, an Indigenous-led advocacy nonprofit based in Rapid City. “We’re people used to being screwed over by the government at every level.”

Don’t miss this: The sadistic online groomers targeting victims around the world

View image in fullscreen Online child exploitation illustration. Illustration: Avinash Weerasekera/The Guardian

This is an incredibly harrowing read about one woman’s attempts to keep her daughter safe from an online predator with ties to the extortion group known as 764. He has been sentenced to decades in prison. We also have this guide to five warning signs for parents about sadistic online exploitation.

… or this: Was Pluto’s 2006 demotion a big mistake?

View image in fullscreen Dwarf planets Ceres, Pluto, and Eris. Photograph: Stocktrek Images, Inc./Alamy

Pluto will always be a planet to me. Tim Dowling explores the debate about its status that continues two decades after it was demoted to being a “dwarf planet”.

Climate check: ‘Breakthrough’ as Turkmenistan starts fixing ‘mindboggling’ methane mega-leaks

View image in fullscreen Flares burn off methane and other hydrocarbons at an oil and gas facility. Photograph: David Goldman/AP

The secretive state has begun repairs on ageing facilities after being revealed as the worst country for leaks of the potent greenhouse gas.

Last Thing: ‘Humongous’ marmot crowned winner in inaugural Fat Marmot Week contest

View image in fullscreen A marmot sitting outside her den. Photograph: Brittany Peterson/AP

Dawn was crowned the winner of the inaugural Fat Marmot Week after securing back-to-back victories in both the mass-gain and popular-vote competitions. The contest was started by researchers who previously turned to OnlyFans to help save a decades-long research project. Go, Dawn!

सुप्रभात। नेपाल केरऽ आधा दर्जन जलविद्युत परियोजना केरऽ सुरंग आरू भूमिगत क्षेत्र म॑ फंसलऽ के आशंका वाला सैकड़ों लोगऽ तक पहुँचै लेली बचाव दल काम करी रहलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि विनाशकारी आकस्मिक बाढ़ के बाद ९०० स॑ अधिक मजदूरऽ के लापता होय के खबर छै ।

पिछला सप्ताह बुधदिन नेपाल के घाटी के माध्यम सं गिरल ⁠अभूतपूर्व बर्फ, चट्टान, थाल आ मलबा के बाढ़ि सं मृतक के संख्या ९०३ भ गेल अछि, जखन कि सीमा के तिब्बत कात १६ गोटे के मौत के खबर अछि. नेपालमे ४ हजारसँ बेसी लापता अछि, तिब्बतमे ५०० गोटे लापता अछि । सैकड़ों लाश, जेकर बहुतो अज्ञात अछि, उथल-पुथल कब्र मे गाड़ल गेल अछि।

बचाव अभियान कतेक पैघ अछि? नेपालक प्रधानमन्त्री बलेन्द्र शाह कहलनि जे, बचाव कार्य मे नागरिक कार्यकर्ता आ स्वयंसेवक के अलावा लगभग २१ हजार सुरक्षाकर्मी सेहो लागल अछि । चीन केरऽ सरकारी सीसीटीवी न॑ खबर देल॑ छै कि बीजिंग न॑ २,१०० स॑ भी अधिक बचावकर्मी क॑ जुटान॑ छै । रेड क्रॉस केरऽ अनुमान छै कि ई आपदा स॑ ९०,००० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ क॑ प्रभावित होय के संभावना छै, जेकरा चीन आरू कुछ विशेषज्ञ न॑ जलवायु संकट केरऽ प्रभाव स॑ जोड़लकै ।

एहि आपदा स ऑस्ट्रेलिया मे जातिवाद क कतार किएक शुरू भ गेल अछि? लापता ऑस्ट्रेलियाई के प्रति सोशल मीडिया पर नस्लवादी टिप्पणी के घेराबंदी करलऽ गेलऽ छै । अधिकांश तीर्थ यात्रा पर छलाह, जाहि मे तिब्बत के कैलाश पर्वत सेहो शामिल छल | न्यूज कॉर्प, चैनल 7, चैनल 10 आरू नाइन सहित मुख्यधारा के मीडिया के फेसबुक पर लापता ऑस्ट्रेलियाई लोगऽ के पहचान करै वाला लेखऽ प॑ बहुत आपत्तिजनक आरू भेदभावपूर्ण टिप्पणी के सामना करना पड़लऽ छै ।

अमेरिका न॑ होर्मुज जलडमरूमध्य म॑ ईरानी लांचर प॑ हमला करलकै, जेकरा स॑ जॉर्डन आरू यूएई केरऽ हवाई अड्डा प॑ जवाबी हमला होय गेलै

फुलस्क्रीन में छवि देखू होर्मुज जलडमरूमध्य के उत्तरी भाग के एकटा विस्तृत दृश्य, जाहि में होरमुज (आर), लाराक (सी), आ केशम (एल) द्वीप देखाओल गेल अछि | फोटोग्राफ: उपग्रह छवि ©2020 मैक्सर टेक/एएफपी/गेटी इमेजेज

ईरान न॑ जॉर्डन आरू संयुक्त अरब अमीरात केरऽ हवाई अड्डा प॑ जवाबी हमला करलकै, जेकरा बाद अमेरिका न॑ होर्मुज जलडमरूमध्य म॑ ईरानी रॉकेट लांचर प॑ हमला करलकै, जे एक महीना म॑ पहलऽ ऐसनऽ दुश्मनी छेकै । ईरान प॑ अमेरिकी हमला केरऽ आखिरी ज्ञात हमला जुलाई के अंत म॑ करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै आरू हाल के हफ्ता म॑ ई युद्ध गतिरोध म॑ पहुँची गेलऽ छै ।

ताजा गोलीबारी के आदान-प्रदान रविदिन देर रात जलडमरूमध्य के लाराक द्वीप पर अमेरिका के हमला सं भेल छल. ईरान केरऽ ⁠क्रांतिकारी गार्ड (आईआरजीसी) न॑ कहलकै कि अमेरिकी हमला म॑ कईएक सैनिक आरू नागरिक के मौत आरू घायल होय गेलै आरू ओकरा तेहरान स॑ “दंड” मिलतै ।

डोनाल्ड ट्रंप अमेरिकी सेना के की करय के दावा केने छथिन्ह? हमला के घंटों बाद अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रंप न॑ सोशल मीडिया पोस्ट म॑ दावा करलकै कि ईरान केरऽ ऊर्जा केंद्र खर्ग द्वीप क॑ “उड़ा देलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै” लेकिन एकरऽ आरू जानकारी नै देलकै । व्हाइट हाउस आरू ⁠अमेरिकी रक्षा विभाग न॑ टिप्पणी करै के आग्रह के तुरंत जवाब नै देलकै । युद्ध स॑ पहल॑ ईरान केरऽ ९०% तेल निर्यात क॑ संभाल॑ वाला खर्ग प॑ हमला करला स॑ इस्लामिक गणराज्य केरऽ ऊर्जा व्यापार म॑ भारी बाधा आबै वाला छै आरू ओकरऽ अर्थव्यवस्था प॑ भारी दबाव पैदा होय जैतै ।

नाम के ल क ट्रंप के साथ थूक बढ़ला के साथ कनाडा न॑ विशालकाय ‘लेक ओंटारियो’ के साइन खड़ा करी देलकै

फुलस्क्रीन में छवि देखें लेक ओंटारियो साइन। फोटोग्राफ : कार्लोस ओसोरिओ/रायटर

डोनाल्ड ट्रंप आरू कनाडा न॑ सप्ताहांत म॑ अमेरिकी सरकार केरऽ ओंटारियो झील केरऽ प्रशासनिक नाम बदलै के मामला म॑ मौखिक द्वंद्वयुद्ध जारी रखलकै, जेकरा म॑ ओन्टारियो केरऽ प्रीमियर न॑ एगो विशालकाय बोर्ड खड़ा करलकै जेकरा प॑ लिखलऽ छेलै “लेक ओंटारियो. अब आरू हमेशा” – आरू अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति न॑ एगो एआई वीडियो पोस्ट करलकै जेकरा म॑ ओकरा वू साइन केरऽ अवतार क॑ तोड़ी क॑ एकरऽ जगह प॑ लेक अमेरिका लिखलऽ गेलऽ छेलै, आरू वाईएमसीए प॑ नाचलऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

वेंडट नेशन केरऽ भव्य प्रमुख पियरे पिकार्ड न॑ ट्रंप केरऽ ई कदम क॑ आदिवासी इतिहास क॑ मिटाबै के कोशिश बतैलकै । पिकार्ड न॑ कहलकै कि हम्में हुनका ई कहना चाहै छियै कि हमरा लेली, एगो राष्ट्र के रूप म॑, एगो ऐसनऽ राष्ट्रपति होना अस्वीकार्य छै जे हमरऽ इतिहास, हमरऽ संस्कृति आरू हमरऽ पहचान क॑ समाप्त करी सक॑ ।

ट्रंप केरऽ ‘सीमा ज़ार’ न॑ इनकार करलकै कि मिलो इयानपोलोस क॑ जल्दी स॑ देश निकाला करी देलऽ गेलै ताकि ओकरा आईसीई हिरासत स॑ बचालऽ जाय सक॑

संघीय आप्रवासन एजेंट द्वारा गिरफ्तारी के बाद मिलो इयानपोलोस | फोटोग्राफ : होमलैंड सुरक्षा विभाग/रायटर

व्हाइट हाउस केरऽ “सीमा ज़ार”, टॉम होमन न॑ रविवार क॑ ई बात स॑ इनकार करलकै कि ब्रिटिश सुदूर दक्षिणपंथी टिप्पणीकार मिलो इयानपोलोस क॑ अमेरिकी आप्रवासन आरू सीमा शुल्क प्रवर्तन (आईसीई) द्वारा गिरफ्तार करला के महज एक दिन बाद देश निकाला करना तरजीही व्यवहार के बराबर छै ।

होमन नँ कहलकै कि ई हुनकऽ समझ छै कि 41 वर्षीय इयानपोलोस जे विजिटर वीजा मान॑ छै, ओकरा स॑ अधिक समय तलक ठहरलऽ छेलै, आप्रवासन के सुनवाई म॑ हाजिर नै छेलै आरू 22 जुलाई क॑ ओकरा हटाबै के अंतिम आदेश जारी करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । ओ आगू कहलनि: “हुनकर उचित प्रक्रिया छलनि, संघीय न्यायाधीश द्वारा हटाबय के आदेश छलनि, आ आईसीई हुनका हटा देलनि.ई एतेक सरल अछि.”

अन्य समाचार मे ...

फुलस्क्रीन एनबीसी के क्रिस्टन वेल्कर में छवि देखू. फोटोग्राफ : जिम बोर्ग/रायटर

डोनाल्ड ट्रंप न॑ कहलकै कि एनबीसी केरऽ क्रिस्टन वेल्कर क॑ एफसीसी स॑ “डांटना या सजा” के सामना करना चाहियऽ, कैन्हेंकि हुनी राजनीतिक उम्मीदवारऽ के सफलता के रिकॉर्ड क॑ “मिश्रित” बतैलकै ।

विशेषज्ञऽ के कहना छै कि राष्ट्रपति केरऽ माफी के अलावा जेफ्री एपस्टीन केरऽ लड़कियऽ आरू युवती सिनी के साथ दुर्व्यवहार म॑ शामिल होय के मामला म॑ अपनऽ सजा क॑ पलटै लेली घिसलेन मैक्सवेल केरऽ कानूनी रास्ता वस्तुतः खतम होय गेलऽ छै ।

full_article:
Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah, an ex-rapper popularly known as "Balen," is facing the enormous task of rebuilding communities and critical infrastructure following last week's deadly flash floods.

The floods, carrying rock, ice, mud and debris, swept through areas near the Chinese border, ravaging entire towns and damaging hydropower plants.

More than 900 people have been killed and nearly 4,800 remain missing, authorities said Monday, as rescue efforts entered a sixth day.

The devastating floods struck the Himalayan nation just days before the anniversary of the Gen-Z-led anti-corruption protests of September 8-9 last year that toppled the previous government and swept Shah to power.

Now, the 36-year-old prime minister and his largely inexperienced cabinet face their first major national crisis in what is shaping up to be the country's worst disaster in a decade.

Anxious relatives await news from flood zone

Rescuers, including Chinese and Indian experts, believe hundreds of workers are trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites under construction that were buried in mud by the catastrophic flooding.

The death toll continued to rise on Monday as increasingly desperate families searched for their loved ones Image: Dar Yasin/AP Photo/picture alliance

Sushila Giri was waiting for news of her son, Sishir, a Kathmandu University student completing an internship at one of the hydropower projects.

"I came to know that my son, along with others, was at the quarter of the hydro project when the disaster happened," she told DW. "Please help me find his whereabouts."

Gen Z activist Raksha Bam expressed concern about delays in rescuing workers trapped at hydropower projects and urged the government to seek specialized assistance from the international community.

Across affected districts, family members gathered in hospitals and temporary aid centers hoping for news of missing loved ones.

Indra Adhikari lost her home and paddy fields in the floods. Four of her relatives remain missing. She said rescue and relief efforts appeared concentrated in areas accessible by road and where media were present, particularly along one side of the Trishuli River.

"Most of those who have come to Trishuli Bazar are not rescuers but onlookers," she told DW. "Remote settlements farther upstream and across the river remain difficult to reach."

How is the new government handling the crisis?

The administration itself has acknowledged that it was not fully prepared for a disaster of such scale, which is the deadliest for Nepal since a 2015 earthquake killed thousands and injured many more.

"On the very first day, we got a bit confused as to how to deal with the crisis," Minister for Information and Communication Bikram Timilsina told DW after visiting the flood-hit area. "[From the] second day onwards, we have been putting all our efforts into swift search, rescue and relief works."

Rescuers have been working to reach hundreds of workers trapped in tunnels of damaged hydropower projects Image: Prime Minister Secretariat, Nepal/AFP

Security agencies have received praise for their response, particularly their efforts to reach people in inaccessible areas via helicopters. But the disaster has also exposed questions about the government's crisis-management capacity and its relationship with Nepal's provincial and local governments.

"Given the scale of devastation, the government's efforts and promptness to deal with the crisis are commendable," Madhu Raman Acharya, a former foreign secretary of Nepal, told DW. "The preliminary search and rescue efforts, especially coordination among security agencies, are commendable."

Govinda Pokharel, a former chief executive officer of the National Reconstruction Authority, which oversaw post-earthquake reconstruction, however, has a different take.

He said that the federal government had attempted to manage the crisis largely on its own, without adequately involving local and provincial governments. This is particularly significant because Shah's ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party has no presence in local or provincial governments.

Pokharel also questioned whether the government's lack of experience had affected its ability to gauge the scale of the response required.

"Our neighboring countries like China and India were willing to lend help for rescue, especially for tunnel-rescue from the very outset," he told DW, adding that the government failed to decide in time whether to allow them to deploy, costing three crucial days.

Can Balen's government deliver?

Nepal initially maintained that its own rescue teams were capable of handling the operation.

But by Friday, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal told the media that the government had decided to seek international expertise, including from China and India, for tunnel rescues, DNA testing and forensic examinations.

The shift highlighted one of the central challenges facing the new administration: whether the government can act quickly and effectively during a rapidly evolving national emergency.

Pokharel said the government's decision to raise substantial funds domestically for disaster relief demonstrated public confidence.

"One good thing is that the government is collecting a huge sum of public money domestically on the Prime Minister's Disaster Relief Fund," he said. "It shows the public trust in the government that doesn't misuse its funds collected in the name of relief."

By Saturday, over 5 billion Nepali rupees ($34.7 million, €29.9 million) had been collected in a government-run disaster relief fund for flood victims, according to the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers.

Prabha Bogati, deputy mayor of Bidur Municipality in Nuwakot, said local authorities had limited scope to act during the crisis because the federal government adopted a centralized "one-door" approach, requiring relief activities to be coordinated through a single command structure.

"In previous crises, local communities and volunteers used to be mobilized in search, rescue and relief efforts," she told DW.

Bogati added that helicopter rescues have been effective, but local stakeholders have not been brought into the response and have not been allowed to recover bodies or perform final rites.

Government spokesperson and Education Minister Sasmit Pokharel defended the administration's response, saying all available resources were being mobilized for rescue, relief and rehabilitation.

"In the first phase, our priority was to save citizens' lives by using the available human resources and means," Pokharel told reporters. "A process has also been initiated to better organize the mobilization of volunteers."

पिछला साल 8-9 सितंबर कए जेन-जेड क नेतृत्व मे भ्रष्टाचार विरोधी विरोध प्रदर्शन क सालगिरह स किछुए दिन पहिने हिमालयी राष्ट्र पर विनाशकारी बाढ़ आयल छल जे पिछला सरकार कए गिरा देलक आ शाह कए सत्ता मे आबि गेल।

आब 36 वर्षीय प्रधानमंत्री आ हुनकर बहुत हद तक अनुभवहीन मंत्रिमंडल कए अपन पहिल पैघ राष्ट्रीय संकट क सामना करय पड़त जे एक दशक मे देश क सबस खराब आपदा क आकार ल रहल अछि।

बेचैन परिजन बाढ़ि क्षेत्र स खबर क इंतजार मे छथि

चीनी आरू भारतीय विशेषज्ञ सहित बचावकर्ता सिनी के मानना छै कि निर्माणाधीन जलविद्युत स्थलऽ प॑ सैकड़ों मजदूर सुरंगऽ म॑ फंसलऽ छै जे विनाशकारी बाढ़ स॑ कीचड़ म॑ दबी गेलऽ छेलै ।

सोमदिन सेहो मृतकक संख्या बढ़ैत रहल, कारण तेजी सं हताश परिवार अपन प्रियजन के खोज मे लागल छल Image: Dar Yasin/AP Photo/picture alliance

सुशीला गिरी अपन बेटा, सिशिर, जे काठमांडू विश्वविद्यालय के छात्रा छल, एकटा जलविद्युत परियोजना मे इंटर्नशिप पूरा करय के खबर के इंतजार मे छलीह.

ओ डीडब्ल्यू स कहली जे हमरा पता चलल जे जखन आपदा आयल छल तखन हमर बेटा दोसर लोक क संग हाइड्रो प्रोजेक्ट क क्वार्टर मे छल। "कृपया हुनकर ठिकाना तकबा मे हमरा मदद करू।"

जेन जेड कार्यकर्ता रक्षा बम न॑ जलविद्युत परियोजना म॑ फंसलऽ मजदूरऽ क॑ बचाबै म॑ देरी के चिंता जतैलकै आरू सरकार स॑ आग्रह करलकै कि अंतरराष्ट्रीय समुदाय स॑ विशेष सहायता लेबै ।

प्रभावित जिला भर मे परिवार के सदस्य अस्पताल आ अस्थायी सहायता केंद्र मे लापता प्रियजन के खबर के उम्मीद मे जमा भ गेलाह.

इन्द्र अधिकारी बाढ़ि मे अपन घर आ धानक खेत गमा लेलनि। हुनकर चारिटा परिजन लापता अछि। हुनी कहलकै कि बचाव आरू राहत के प्रयास सड़कऽ स॑ पहुँचै वाला इलाका आरू जहां मीडिया मौजूद छै, खास करी क॑ त्रिशुली नदी के एक तरफ म॑ केंद्रित नजर आबी रहलऽ छै ।

ओ डीडब्ल्यू स कहली जे त्रिशुली बाजार मे जे लोक आयल छथि ओहि मे स बेसीतर बचावकर्ता नहि बल्कि देखनिहार छथि। "दूर ऊपर आ नदी के ओहि पार दूरस्थ बस्ती तक पहुंचब मुश्किल बनल अछि."

नव सरकार संकट के कोना संभालि रहल अछि?

प्रशासन स्वयं स्वीकार केलक अछि जे ओ एहन पैमाना पर आफत के लेल पूर्ण रूप स तैयार नहि छल, जे नेपाल लेल सबस घातक अछि, जखन कि 2015 मे आयल भूकंप मे हजारों लोक के मौत आ कतेको गोटे घायल भेल छल।

सूचना आ संचार मंत्री बिक्रम तिमिलसिना बाढ़ि प्रभावित इलाका के दौरा के बाद डीडब्ल्यू के कहलनि जे, पहिल दिन हम सब कनि भ्रमित भ गेलहुं जे संकट सं कोना निपटल जाय। "[दोसरऽ दिन स॑ ही] हम्मं॑ अपनऽ सब प्रयास तेजी स॑ खोज, बचाव आरू राहत कार्य म॑ लगाय रहलऽ छियै ।"

क्षतिग्रस्त जलविद्युत परियोजना के सुरंग मे फंसल सैकड़ों मजदूर तक पहुंचेबा लेल बचावकर्मी काज करैत आबि रहल अछि छवि: प्रधानमंत्री सचिवालय, नेपाल/एएफपी

सुरक्षा एजेंसी सब क॑ हुनकऽ प्रतिक्रिया खास करी क॑ हेलीकॉप्टर के माध्यम स॑ दुर्गम क्षेत्रऽ म॑ लोगऽ तलक पहुँचै के कोशिश के प्रशंसा मिललऽ छै । लेकिन आपदा स॑ सरकार केरऽ संकट-प्रबन्धन क्षमता आरू नेपाल केरऽ प्रांतीय आरू स्थानीय सरकारऽ स॑ ओकरऽ संबंध के बारे म॑ भी सवाल सामने ऐलऽ छै ।

नेपालक पूर्व विदेश सचिव मधुरमन आचार्य डीडब्ल्यू केँ कहलनि जे, तबाहीक पैमाना केँ देखैत सरकारक प्रयास आ संकट सँ निपटबाक शीघ्रता सराहनीय अछि। "प्रारंभिक खोज आरू बचाव के प्रयास, खास करी क सुरक्षा एजेंसी के बीच समन्वय सराहनीय छै।"

भूकंप के बाद पुनर्निर्माण के देखरेख करय वाला राष्ट्रीय पुनर्निर्माण प्राधिकरण के पूर्व मुख्य कार्यकारी अधिकारी गोविंदा पोखरेल के नजरिया हालांकि अलग अछि.

ओ कहलनि जे, संघीय सरकार स्थानीय आ प्रांतीय सरकार के पर्याप्त रूप स शामिल नहि केने, संकट के बहुत हद तक अपन दम पर प्रबंधित करबाक प्रयास केलक अछि। ई खास करी क॑ महत्वपूर्ण छै, कैन्हेंकि शाह केरऽ सत्तारूढ़ राष्ट्रीय स्वतंत्र पार्टी केरऽ स्थानीय या प्रांतीय सरकारऽ म॑ कोय मौजूदगी नै छै ।

पोखरेल न॑ ई भी सवाल उठैलकै कि की सरकार केरऽ अनुभव के कमी स॑ ओकरऽ जरूरत के प्रतिक्रिया के पैमाना के आकलन करै के क्षमता प॑ असर पड़लै ।

हुनी डीडब्ल्यू स॑ कहलकै कि चीन आरू भारत जैसनऽ हमरऽ पड़ोसी देश शुरू स॑ ही बचाव लेली मदद दै लेली तैयार छेलै, खास करी क॑ सुरंग-बचाव लेली ।

नेपाल में सैकड़ों ⁠बाढ़ पीड़ित के सामूहिक दफन शुरू भेल ई वीडियो देखबाक लेल कृपया जावास्क्रिप्ट सक्षम करू, आ HTML5 वीडियो के सपोर्ट करय वाला वेब ब्राउजर में अपग्रेड करय पर विचार करू

की बालेन के सरकार डिलीवर क सकैत अछि?

नेपाल शुरू मे अपन बचाव दल अभियान सम्हारबा मे सक्षम रहल कहैत छल ।

लेकिन शुक्रवार तलक विदेश मंत्री शिशिर खनाल नँ मीडिया स॑ कहलकै कि सरकार न॑ सुरंग बचाव, डीएनए जांच आरू फोरेंसिक जांच लेली चीन आरू भारत सहित अंतरराष्ट्रीय विशेषज्ञता लेबै के फैसला करलकै ।

ई बदलाव न॑ नयका प्रशासन के सामने एगो केंद्रीय चुनौती प॑ प्रकाश डाललकै कि की सरकार तेजी स॑ विकसित होय रहलऽ राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल के दौरान जल्दी आरू प्रभावी ढंग स॑ काम करी सकै छै ।

पोखरेल कहलनि जे, सरकार द्वारा आपदा राहत लेल घरेलू स्तर पर पर्याप्त धन जुटेबाक निर्णय जनविश्वास के दर्शाबैत अछि।

ओ कहला जे एकटा नीक गप इ अछि जे सरकार प्रधानमंत्री आपदा राहत कोष पर घरेलू स्तर पर सार्वजनिक राशि क भारी राशि क संग्रह क रहल अछि। "ई सरकार पर जन विश्वास के दर्शाबै छै जे राहत के नाम पर जमा करलौ गेलौ धन के दुरुपयोग नै करै छै।"

प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालय आ मन्त्रिपरिषद्के अनुसार शनिदिन बाढि पीडितके लेल सरकारी आपदा राहत कोषमे ५ अरब नेपाली रुपैया (३४.७ मिलियन डॉलर, २९.९ मिलियन यूरो) सँ बेसी संग्रहण भऽ चुकल अछि ।

नुवाकोट के बिदुर नगरपालिका के डिप्टी मेयर प्रभा बोगाटी के कहनाय छनि जे संकट के दौरान स्थानीय प्राधिकरण के काज करय के गुंजाइश सीमित अछि किएक त संघीय सरकार केंद्रीकृत “एक दरवाजा” के तरीका अपना लेलक अछि, जाहि मे राहत गतिविधि के एकहि कमान संरचना के माध्यम सं समन्वय करय के जरूरत अछि.

ओ डीडब्ल्यू कए कहली जे पिछला संकट मे स्थानीय समुदाय आ स्वयंसेवक कए खोज, बचाव आ राहत प्रयास मे जुटाउल जाइत छल।

बोगाटी न॑ आरू कहलकै कि हेलीकॉप्टर स॑ बचाव प्रभावी रहलऽ छै, लेकिन स्थानीय हितधारकऽ क॑ प्रतिक्रिया म॑ नै लानलऽ गेलऽ छै आरू ओकरा लाश बरामद करै या अंतिम संस्कार करै के अनुमति नै देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

सरकार के प्रवक्ता आ शिक्षा मंत्री सस्मित पोखरेल प्रशासन के प्रतिक्रिया के बचाव करैत कहलनि जे, बचाव, राहत आ पुनर्वास के लेल उपलब्ध सब संसाधन जुटाओल जा रहल अछि।

पोखरेल पत्रकार सब सं बातचीत मे कहलनि जे, पहिल चरण मे हमर प्राथमिकता उपलब्ध मानव संसाधन आ साधन के उपयोग क नागरिक के जान बचाबय के छल। "स्वयंसेवक के जुटान के बेहतर आयोजन के लेल एकटा प्रक्रिया सेहो शुरू कएल गेल अछि."

नेपाल में परिवार आशा स चिपकल अछि कियाक त हजारों एखनो गायब अछि ई वीडियो देखबाक लेल कृपया जावास्क्रिप्ट सक्षम करू, आ HTML5 वीडियो के समर्थन करय वाला वेब ब्राउजर में अपग्रेड करय पर विचार करू

title: Nepal flood rescue recovery efforts keep hope alive for some, but not all, as 4,200 people remain missing - CBS News
description: Nepal flood rescue recovery efforts keep hope alive for some, but not all, as 4,200 people remain missing  CBS News
publisher.title: CBS News
full_article:
Kathmandu, Nepal — Five days after a rocky mountainside and the glacier it supported collapsed near Nepal's border with Tibet, unleashing torrents of flash floodwater , mud and debris on the valleys below that swept away everything in their path, rescuers were still searching Monday for reasons to hope.

Over the weekend, a 6-year-old girl was miraculously pulled from the mud-covered rubble, fueling hope that more of the 4,200 people still listed as missing in the wake of the disaster could be found alive.

Nepal's national disaster agency said Monday that at least 903 people had been killed, and the fear is that the toll will spiral as recovery efforts continue along the scars carved into the landscape by the raging floods.

But the danger hasn't passed. The sacred Trishuli River was surging again Monday , this time from heavy monsoon rains that have spurred search and rescue teams to try and move even faster to find anyone still alive in the ruins.

Deadly Nepal floods highlight glacier risks in warming Himalayas

Nepal Army soldiers work during a search and rescue operation near the Trishuli Hydropower Project site, following deadly flash floods and mudslides, in Rasuwa district, Nepal, in a handout photo obtained by Reuters, Aug. 31, 2026. Nepal Army/Handout/REUTERS

Samarth Srivastav was among the thousands of people desperately hoping a loved one might still emerge from the layers of thick mud and rubble in the Himalayan valleys.

"We're just trying to hope for good news now," Samarth told CBS News from Atlanta.

His father Vivek was on the Nepal-Tibet border when the disaster struck last week.

Samarth said his father joked with him on their last phone call about how steep the river valley walls around him were, saying, "You know, if I fall down there, like, I'll get swept away."

Just hours after the call, a tsunami of glacial ice, water and mud swept away Tibet's immigration checkpoint on the border, and Vivek hasn't been heard from since.

A file Vantor satellite image, above, shows the Gyirong Port border post facility on the China-Nepal border in April 2024, while another Vantor image taken on Aug. 27, 2026, below, shows the same area after flash floods swept through the valley on the preceding morning. Satellite images (c) 2026 Vantor/Getty

"Initially after hearing about it, you know, it was kind of like, okay, you know, maybe by the end of the day, you know? Might hear something back. And then the next day came and we didn't hear anything all day. And then more and more," he said. "As the number of missing people on record started to increase and, like, the severity of the situation actually started to hit, you know — we're seeing all these videos pop up on social media of people recording the disaster and everything that actually happened — I think that's when we actually started to get worried and realize that something might actually be wrong. This is actually a really bad situation."

Since then, Samarth said it has been nothing but "increasing anxiety" for his family.

"We still have the hope that he's probably okay — he's able to come back, he's probably doing fine out there," he said. "But, it's the fact we don't know anything yet, is just so scary to us."

The torrents of floodwater and everything they picked up and carried with them pushed as far as 150 miles away, into neighboring India.

At Nepal's biggest hospital, in the capital Kathmandu, an outside wall has been all but covered in posters bearing the photos of bodies recovered from the calamity. Another wall, on a smaller street nearby, was starting to fill up Monday.

They are walls of the unknown dead — photos of some of the people still likely listed as missing.

Families and relatives of missing persons from the Tibet-Nepal floods view images of bodies displayed on a wall of the Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu, Nepal, Aug. 30, 2026. Subaas Shrestha/NurPhoto/Getty

Many of the images are deeply disturbing, but desperate family members have no choice but to step up to pore over the grim images, pleading for any information about missing loved ones.

In Georgia, Samarth said he was trying to keep calm, despite a lack of any information from officials in Nepal, or at home in the U.S.

"Honestly, I haven't really heard as much from the U.S. government," he said. "There's not really much else we can do except just, like, sit and pray."

Other American families with loved ones missing told CBS News over the weekend that they want more help from U.S. authorities, as well as the Chinese and Nepalese governments.

One family in Virginia told CBS News on Monday that they had given up hope, and they have now started mourning for their mother and father, who they believe were in Tibet when the floods hit.

title: The Nepal floods seem a world away – but make no mistake, climate breakdown will affect us all | Nesrine Malik - The Guardian
description: The Nepal floods seem a world away – but make no mistake, climate breakdown will affect us all | Nesrine Malik  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
C limate breakdown is happening on one Earth, but two different worlds. In one, its impacts increasingly encroach on everyday life; longer periods of discomfort and shorter periods of sharp pain. Endless, hotter summers, and within them sudden wildfires, evacuations, homes burned to cinders in a matter of hours. In another, catastrophe. This summer has been a snapshot of that split-screen. The hottest day on record in parts of Europe, and a wave of water, mud and ice in Nepal that so far has claimed more than 750 lives. Thousands of people are still missing.

The difference is also one of resources. The climate crisis has an economic cost, but some places can absorb it better than others. Responses to this summer of wildfires in Europe included a rapid scrambling by the French government to provide everything from tax breaks for businesses affected by the fires to relocation costs and aid to rebuild homes. The UK government had deployed almost £100m before the summer to strengthen wildfire resilience.

Entire industries exist to absorb the impact, undergirded by sophisticated technology, disposable income and evolved sectors. Wildfire insurance in the US is being powered by AI, which spits out numbers to estimate risk based on location and construction material. Outside North America and Europe, there is little of that buffer. The result is asymmetry. While developed countries will still be stressed as events triggered by climate breakdown become more regular and chronic, and they are still not immune to globalised outcomes – rising food costs, droughts, water shortages – what they experience and how disruptive that will be are far removed from other parts of the world.

The difference in scale and resources is colossal. What is needed to rebuild Nepal’s flood damage may constitute up to a 10th of its entire economy – something like $5bn, and that’s not even factoring in all the technical foreign assistance, equipment, expertise and labour required. Also colossal is the difference in exposure to the obliterative effects of events.

Take the death of coral reefs, and how that disproportionately affects coastal populations. Across the Caribbean, coral bleaching caused by rising ocean acidification and temperatures not only dramatically reduces marine life, which is a source of food and income for entire populations – 90% of Jamaica’s economic income is generated alongside its coasts – but also increases the scale and intensity of storms. Coral reefs are a sort of natural storm barrier, absorbing the force of sea waves and buffering coastal areas from flooding. The intersection between these geographical and economic features means countries in the Caribbean are being pummelled on the weather front (climate breakdown also increases the power of hurricanes through warming ocean water), as well as having their incomes drastically reduced and therefore their ability to bounce back.

Then there is the heat. Temperatures are not just jumping far above the average in Europe but also in warmer areas where the base temperatures are already high. Last week, a Harper’s Index summary of estimated heat-related mortality in India showed some staggering numbers: 3,400 excess deaths “caused by a single day of extreme heat”; 30,000 deaths “caused by five consecutive days of extreme heat”. In April of this year, all 50 of the world’s hottest cities were in a single country, India, something which according to the air-quality monitoring platform AQI “has no modern precedent across global weather data”.

2:04 ‘I have lost everything’: survivors reflect after deadly flood in Nepal – video

This is another double whammy for poor communities without access to shelter or cooling systems of unlimited fresh water. These are the so-called climate breakdown hotspots, identified as “areas where strong physical and ecological effects of climate change come together with large numbers of vulnerable and poor people and communities”. Few places on Earth demonstrate this category more vividly than Sudan. A country already in the grip of war and food insecurity is now succumbing to the delayed rains caused by the El Niño climate pattern, cracking the dry earth and draining the Nile. The risk of famine stalks populations that are already acutely hungry.

And what is felt asymmetrically has been caused in that way too. These poorer, more vulnerable countries are paying the price for the emissions caused by wealthy countries, and not even being extended the full, remedial support from the coffers of those nations that accumulated the wealth generated by industries that contributed to climate breakdown and global heating. We are not just battling complacency, or indifference to the importance of climate justice, but a political climate that has in recent years, led by Donald Trump’s second term, seen its own collapse.

Look closer and the problem isn’t only historical failure but a casual disregard, an adventurism that launches wars and stresses economies with buffers already damaged by the climate crisis. The Iran war in combination with El Niño is a weather and politics collaboration that has hiked fertiliser costs on the one hand and choked rain on the other. More broadly, what was a generously named albeit tenuously implemented “rules-based order”, which at least had some bedrock of global cooperation and aid, has been cancelled altogether. Trump’s withdrawal from the Paris agreement set the tone, while the dismantling of USAID cut the funds that diverted billions of dollars from the rich to the developing world to help with the fallout of extreme weather and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

Here is another cascade. As the US withdraws from its commitments, sending the signal that there are no rules or duties, and indeed no problem with climate breakdown at all, pressure will rise on other countries to contribute more. They will need to figure out a way to hold together a coordinated response in the shadow of a destabilising hegemon, as well as try to foster that sense of social obligation in a time of political sociopathy.

The foolish shortsightedness of it all is that even though there is a large gap between experiences, and so a sense that glaciers and floods and famines are happening all the way over there, their knock-on effects and food supply challenges, and political and refugee crises, will affect us all. Things will get dramatically worse for the hotspots, but there is still no outrunning it all in the long term. It seems that at precisely the moment when this realisation should yoke us together in all the ways life is rapidly changing, we are all being untethered. But ultimately, whatever different spheres we inhabit, we are all still trapped on the same planet.

C limate breakdown एक पृथ्वी पर भ रहल अछि, मुदा दू अलग-अलग दुनिया पर | एकटा में एकर प्रभाव रोजमर्रा के जीवन में तेजी सं अतिक्रमण करैत अछि; बेसी काल असुविधा आ कम समय मे तेज दर्द। अंतहीन, गरम गर्मी, आ ओकर भीतर अचानक जंगली आगि, खाली करब, घर घंटों में जरि कए सिंडर भ गेल. दोसर मे प्रलय। ई गर्मी ओहि स्प्लिट-स्क्रीन के स्नैपशॉट रहल अछि. यूरोप केरऽ कुछ हिस्सा म॑ रिकॉर्ड म॑ सबस॑ गरम दिन, आरू नेपाल म॑ पानी, थाल आरू बर्फ केरऽ लहर जेकरा म॑ अखनी तलक ७५० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के जान गेलऽ छै । हजारों लोक एखनो लापता अछि।

अंतर संसाधनक सेहो अछि। जलवायु संकट के आर्थिक लागत छै, लेकिन कुछ जगह एकरा दोसरऽ जगहऽ स॑ बेहतर ढंग स॑ आत्मसात करी सकै छै । यूरोप म॑ ई गर्मी म॑ जंगली आग केरऽ जवाब म॑ फ्रांस सरकार केरऽ तेजी स॑ दौड़-धूप शामिल छेलै कि आगि स॑ प्रभावित व्यवसायी लेली करऽ म॑ छूट स॑ ल॑ क॑ स्थानांतरण केरऽ लागत आरू घरऽ के पुनर्निर्माण म॑ सहायता तक उपलब्ध कराय देलऽ गेलै । ब्रिटेन सरकार न॑ गर्मी स॑ पहल॑ लगभग १०० मिलियन पाउंड के तैनाती करी क॑ जंगली आग के प्रतिरोधक क्षमता क॑ मजबूत करी देल॑ छेलै ।

परिष्कृत तकनीक, प्रयोज्य आय आ विकसित क्षेत्रक कें आधार पर प्रभाव कें आत्मसात करय कें लेल पूरा उद्योग मौजूद छै. अमेरिका म॑ जंगली आग के बीमा क॑ एआई द्वारा संचालित करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै, जे स्थान आरू निर्माण सामग्री के आधार प॑ जोखिम के अनुमान लगाबै लेली संख्या थूकै छै । उत्तरी अमेरिका आ यूरोप सं बाहर ओहि बफरक कम अछि. परिणाम विषमता होइत अछि। जखन कि विकसित देशक कें एखनहु तनाव होयत, कियाकि जलवायु टूटय सं शुरू भेल घटनाक नियमित आ पुरान भ जायत छै, आ ओ एखनहु वैश्वीकरण कें परिणाम सं अछूत नहि छै – बढ़ैत खाद्य लागत, सूखा, पानी कें कमी – ओकरा की अनुभव होयत छै आ जे कतेक विघटनकारी होयत, दुनिया कें अन्य भागक सं बहुत दूर छै.

पैमाना आ संसाधन मे अंतर बहुत पैघ अछि। नेपाल केरऽ बाढ़ केरऽ नुकसान केरऽ पुनर्निर्माण लेली जे जरूरत छै, वू ओकरऽ पूरा अर्थव्यवस्था केरऽ दसवां हिस्सा तक होय सकै छै – कुछ ५ अरब डॉलर जैसनऽ, आरू ई सब तकनीकी विदेशी सहायता, उपकरण, विशेषज्ञता आरू श्रम केरऽ जरूरत केरऽ कारक तक नै मानलऽ जाय छै । संगहि घटनाक विनाशकारी प्रभावक संपर्क मे एबाक अंतर सेहो विशाल अछि ।

कोरल रीफक मृत्यु कें लिय , आ से तटीय आबादी पर कोना अनुपातहीन प्रभाव पड़ैत छैक. कैरेबियन भर म॑ बढ़तऽ समुद्र केरऽ अम्लीकरण आरू तापमान के कारण कोरल ब्लीचिंग स॑ न सिर्फ समुद्री जीवन म॑ नाटकीय रूप स॑ कमी ​​आबै छै, जे पूरा आबादी लेली भोजन आरू आय के स्रोत छै – जमैका केरऽ ९०% आर्थिक आय ओकरऽ तट के साथ-साथ पैदा होय छै – बल्कि तूफान केरऽ पैमाना आरू तीव्रता म॑ भी वृद्धि करै छै । कोरल रीफ एक तरह के प्राकृतिक तूफान बाधा छै, जे समुद्री लहरऽ के बल क॑ सोख॑ छै आरू तटीय क्षेत्रऽ क॑ बाढ़ स॑ बफर करै छै । ई भौगोलिक आरू आर्थिक विशेषता के बीच के चौराहा के मतलब छै कि कैरेबियन देशऽ क॑ मौसम के मोर्चा प॑ पम्मेल करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै (जलवायु टूटला स॑ समुद्र केरऽ पानी क॑ गरम होय के माध्यम स॑ तूफान केरऽ शक्ति भी बढ़ी जाय छै), साथ ही साथ ओकरऽ आमदनी म॑ भारी कमी आबी गेलऽ छै आरू ई लेली ओकरऽ वापस उछली के क्षमता भी बढ़ी जाय छै ।

तखन तऽ गर्मी। यूरोप केरऽ तापमान औसत स॑ बहुत ऊपर ही नै उछली रहलऽ छै बल्कि गर्म क्षेत्रऽ म॑ भी जहाँ आधार तापमान पहिने स॑ ही अधिक छै । पिछला सप्ताह भारत में गर्मी सं जुड़ल अनुमानित मृत्यु दरक हार्पर इंडेक्स केर सारांश में किछु डगमगाइत संख्या देखबा में आयल : 3,400 अतिरिक्त मृत्यु “एक दिनक अत्यधिक गर्मी सं” ; 30,000 मौत “लगभग पांच दिन के अत्यधिक गर्मी के कारण”। ई साल अप्रैल म॑ दुनिया केरऽ सब ५० सबसें गरम शहर एक ही देश भारत म॑ छेलै, जे हवा के गुणवत्ता निगरानी प्लेटफॉर्म एक्यूआई के अनुसार “वैश्विक मौसम केरऽ आंकड़ा म॑ कोनो आधुनिक मिसाल नै छै” ।

2:04 ‘हम सब किछु गमा लेलहुँ’: नेपाल मे घातक बाढ़िक बाद बचि गेल लोक चिंतन – वीडियो

इ गरीब समुदायक कें लेल एकटा आ दोहरा झटका छै, जेकरा मे आश्रय या असीमित मीठा पानी कें शीतलन प्रणाली कें पहुंच नहि छै. इ तथाकथित जलवायु टूटय कें हॉटस्पॉट छै, जेकर पहचान “ओह क्षेत्रक कें रूप मे कैल गेल छै जतय जलवायु परिवर्तन कें मजबूत भौतिक आ पारिस्थितिक प्रभाव पैघ संख्या मे कमजोर आ गरीब लोगक आ समुदायक कें साथ मिल क आबै छै” । पृथ्वी पर सूडान सं बेसी एहि श्रेणी के बेसी सजीव रूप सं प्रदर्शन करय वाला जगह कम अछि. जे देश पहिने स॑ ही युद्ध आरू खाद्य असुरक्षा के चपेट म॑ छै, वू अब॑ एल नीनो जलवायु पैटर्न के वजह स॑ देरी स॑ होय वाला बारिश के सामना करी रहलऽ छै, जेकरा स॑ शुष्क धरती म॑ दरार आबी रहलऽ छै आरू नील नदी के पानी निकली गेलऽ छै । अकाल कें खतरा ओ आबादी कें डंठल करएयत छै जे पहिने सं तीव्र भूखल छै.

आ जे असममित रूपेँ महसूस होइत अछि से ओहि तरहेँ सेहो भेल अछि । ई गरीब, अधिक कमजोर देशऽ के कीमत अमीर देशऽ द्वारा होय वाला उत्सर्जन के कीमत चुकाबै छै, आरू वू राष्ट्रऽ के खजाना स॑ पूरा, सुधारात्मक समर्थन तक नै बढ़ालऽ जाय रहलऽ छै जे जलवायु टूटना आरू वैश्विक ताप म॑ योगदान दै वाला उद्योगऽ स॑ पैदा होय वाला धन क॑ जमा करलकै । हम खाली आत्मसंतोष, या जलवायु न्याय के महत्व के प्रति उदासीनता स॑ नै लड़ै छियै, बल्कि एगो ऐसनऽ राजनीतिक माहौल जेकरा म॑ हाल के सालऽ म॑ डोनाल्ड ट्रंप केरऽ दोसरऽ कार्यकाल के नेतृत्व म॑ अपनऽ पतन देखलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

करीब स’ देखू आ समस्या मात्र ऐतिहासिक असफलता नहिं अपितु आकस्मिक अवहेलना अछि, एकटा साहसिकता जे युद्ध शुरू करैत अछि आ जलवायु संकट सं पहिने सं क्षतिग्रस्त बफर वाला अर्थव्यवस्था पर जोर दैत अछि. एल नीनो के संयोजन म॑ ईरान युद्ध मौसम आरू राजनीति के सहयोग छेकै जेकरा स॑ एक तरफ खाद के लागत बढ़ी गेलऽ छै आरू दोसरऽ तरफ बारिश के गला घोंटलऽ छै । अधिक व्यापक रूप स॑ कहलऽ जाय त॑ जेकरा क॑ उदारता स॑ नाम देलऽ गेलऽ छेलै हालांकि क्षीण रूप स॑ लागू करलऽ गेलऽ “नियम आधारित आदेश” छेलै, जेकरा म॑ कम स॑ कम वैश्विक सहयोग आरू सहायता केरऽ कुछ आधारशिला छेलै, ओकरा एकदम रद्द करी देलऽ गेलऽ छै । पेरिस समझौता स॑ ट्रंप केरऽ वापसी न॑ सुर तय करलकै, जबकि यूएसएआईडी केरऽ भंग करला स॑ वू धनराशि म॑ कटौती होय गेलै जेकरा स॑ अरबों डॉलर के धन क॑ अमीरऽ स॑ विकासशील दुनिया म॑ मोड़लऽ गेलै ताकि चरम मौसम केरऽ परिणाम म॑ मदद मिल॑ सक॑ आरू ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जन क॑ कम करलऽ जाय सक॑ ।
